title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §15 of the 'Longue Marche' sequel (ms. pp. 732–733). On the previous page Grothendieck fixes a rational prime p and an ℓ-adic Kummer character ζ_{p,ℓ}. It comes from the Kummer tower of x ↦ x^{ℓ^ν} on G_m, with inverse images of p ∈ G_m(Q). In general this is only a 1-cocycle Γ_Q → Z_ℓ(1). On Γ_Q^+ = ∩_{ℓ'} Ker χ_{ℓ'}, where all cyclotomic characters are trivial, it becomes a homomorphism Γ_Q^+ → Z_ℓ(1). He wants to know whether these characters are surjective, or at least surjective for all but finitely many ℓ.

To localize the question he uses:
- the decomposition group D_ℓ = Gal(Q̄_ℓ/Q_ℓ) and its inertia subgroup I_ℓ;
- I_ℓ^+ := Ker(χ_ℓ|I_ℓ). This lies in Γ_Q^+ because inertia at ℓ acts trivially on μ_{ℓ'^∞} for ℓ' ≠ ℓ. Concretely, I_ℓ^+ = Gal(Q̄_ℓ / Q_ℓ^{ur}(μ_{ℓ^∞})).

This page states (365): restrict ζ_{p,ℓ} to I_ℓ^+ → Ẑ_ℓ(1) = Z_ℓ(1). It asks whether this local homomorphism is surjective, or at least has open image. The question is left unanswered. The next page breaks off to §16, 'Réflexions sur le théorème de Fermat'.

Modern answer, by local Kummer theory over K = Q_ℓ^{ur}(μ_{ℓ^∞}), ℓ odd:
- Case p = ℓ. Q_ℓ(μ_{ℓ^∞}, ℓ^{1/ℓ^∞}) has Galois group Z_ℓ(1) ⋊ Z_ℓ^*, and adjoining the unramified closure does not shrink the Kummer part. So the restriction is surjective.
- Case p ≠ ℓ. Write p = ω·u with ω ∈ μ_{ℓ-1} and u ∈ 1+ℓZ_ℓ. The ω part has all ℓ-power roots in Q_ℓ, so only u matters, and u = (1+ℓ)^{ℓ^m·unit} with m = v_ℓ(p^{ℓ-1}−1) − 1.
- (1+ℓ) is not an ℓ-th power in K. Q_ℓ(μ_ℓ,(1+ℓ)^{1/ℓ}) is ramified over Q_ℓ(μ_ℓ), since 1+ℓ ≡ 1 exactly mod λ^{ℓ−1}. Its Galois group over Q_ℓ is non-abelian, whereas Q_ℓ^{ur}(μ_{ℓ^∞}) is abelian over Q_ℓ, so it cannot lie inside K.
- Hence image(ζ_{p,ℓ}|I_ℓ^+) = ℓ^{m} Z_ℓ(1). It is always open.
- It is surjective iff p^{ℓ−1} ≢ 1 mod ℓ², i.e. iff ℓ is not a Wieferich prime to base p.

Globally, ζ_{p,ℓ}: Γ_Q^+ → Z_ℓ(1) is surjective for every odd ℓ. Since Q(p^{1/ℓ}) is not abelian over Q, p is not an ℓ-th power in Q(μ_∞). It fails for ℓ = 2, where √p ∈ Q(μ_∞) and the image has index 2. So the hope of 'surjective except for finitely many ℓ' on the previous page is true, with ℓ = 2 the only exception. The refined, inertia-local surjectivity for almost all ℓ is equivalent to there being only finitely many Wieferich primes to base p. That is an open problem; even infinitude of non-Wieferich primes is known only conditionally, via abc (Silverman 1988). Note the juxtaposition with the immediately following Fermat section: Wieferich's criterion for the first case of FLT.
errors: No error on the page itself; it only poses a question.
Writing Ẑ_ℓ(1) is harmless notation for Z_ℓ(1).
Implicitly one needs ℓ odd for the clean statements; for ℓ = 2 the global Kummer character has index-2 image.

ideas.what: Restriction of the ℓ-adic Kummer character of a rational prime p to I_ℓ^+, the inertia subgroup at ℓ inside the kernel of all cyclotomic characters; question of surjectivity / openness of the image.
ideas.modern_name: Local Kummer theory over Q_ℓ^{ur}(μ_{ℓ^∞}); image of Kummer characters on inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Kummer, Hasse); standard in Iwasawa theory and in work on Kummer towers in p-adic Hodge theory

ideas.what: Using the subgroup Γ_Q^+ (kernel of the full cyclotomic character), on which Kummer cocycles become homomorphisms, to study Galois action on the Kummer tower of G_m — part of his study of Γ_Q acting on tori / Fermat towers.
ideas.modern_name: Kummer characters on Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_∞)); Ihara/Deligne-style Kummer and Soulé characters
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Deligne (1980s) for the profinite/pro-ℓ GT setting

missed.claim: The local question posed here (surjectivity of ζ_{p,ℓ} on I_ℓ^+) is exactly the non-Wieferich condition p^{ℓ−1} ≢ 1 mod ℓ². The image always has index ℓ^{v_ℓ(p^{ℓ−1}−1)−1}. Grothendieck poses it on the page immediately before beginning 'Réflexions sur le théorème de Fermat', where Wieferich-type congruences classically arise. He does not make the link explicitly.
missed.quote: on peut se demander déjà si cet homomorphisme est surjectif, ou si du moins son image est ouverte ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly of historical interest: the answer is standard local Kummer theory. It shows his 'surjective for almost all ℓ' hope, in its inertia-local form, hits the open finiteness question for Wieferich primes.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a short, natural question whose answer (open image; surjective iff non-Wieferich) follows from routine local Kummer theory. The only mild interest is the implicit link to Wieferich primes, just before the Fermat section.
transcription_corrections: Machine transcription is essentially correct. The target is written Ẑ_ℓ(1) with a hat (i.e. Z_ℓ(1)). The character is ζ_{p,ℓ}, the same symbol the previous page's transcription renders as 'Σ_{p,e}'.
